about: Things that happen around this family, for the hackathon day (Saturday 21 November 2026). Each signal says which moment it is (market, rule, life or decision), whether it is simulated (invented for the exercise) or comes from the family's plan or an official source, what it touches in this family's plan, and where in the case data to look. Simulated events are not real news. Amounts are US dollars.

signals.headline: AI chip stocks sell off: Nvidia down 30% in two weeks
signals.what_happened: Simulated. Nvidia has fallen 30% in two weeks. Since 6 November the Nasdaq 100 is down 12% and the S&P 500 is down 8%. Commentators ask whether the AI bubble is bursting.
touches_this_family: Technology is 35.6% of Daniel and Emily's stock holdings, mostly through VTI.

Closest past shock in the data: when the Liberation Day tariffs were announced (2 Apr 2025) this portfolio fell 8.1%, against 7.8% for a simple mix with the same stock share. A fall that size today would be about $27,800 on $344,000 of investments and cash.
Worst fall in the last three years: 10.0%, recovered in 61 days.
Longer history: in the Global Financial Crisis (Oct 2007 to Mar 2009) the current mix would have lost 20.4% and the recommended mix 9.9%; in the COVID crash (Feb to Mar 2020) 12.6% and 12.7%.
The 529 college account holds $25,000 of VWO (emerging-market stocks) and $5,000 of cash (positions).

signals.headline: 2027 tax values published: standard deduction, brackets, child tax credit, Social Security wage base
signals.what_happened: The IRS published the 2027 inflation adjustments on 5 November 2026: standard deduction $16,600 single and $33,200 married filing jointly (from $16,100 and $32,200), brackets indexed, child tax credit $2,300 per child (from $2,200). The Social Security wage base rises to $192,300 for 2027 (from $184,500). They apply from 1 January 2027.
touches_this_family: Married filing jointly: standard deduction rises by $1,000, from $32,200 to $33,200.
Child tax credit rises by $100 per child for Oliver (11) and Sophia (9): $200 a year more; their $280,000 of salaries is below the $400,000 phase-out start.
Both salaries ($160,000 and $120,000) are below the wage base, so the Social Security change does not raise their payroll tax.
where_in_the_data: legal-values.json (same file as legal/legal-dataset-sample.json): StandardDeductionByYear, FederalIncomeTaxBracketsByYear, ChildTaxCreditByYear, SSWageBaseByYear
sources: SSA contribution and benefit base 2027: $192,300 (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html; 2027 COLA fact sheet https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html)

signals.headline: Oliver turns 12 next week
signals.what_happened: Simulated date (the plan has his age, not his birthday). Oliver turns 12 on 27 November. His college starts in August 2033, a little under seven years away.
touches_this_family: College goal: $60,000 per child; Oliver in August 2033, Sophia in August 2035 (persona D1, subjective concerns).
A $106,552 college gap remains after the $30,000 already in the 529, even with $8,000 a year going in (persona O8).
The 529 receives $8,000 a year while retirement accounts receive nothing (persona T5).
Decision style: dual. Emily holds the savings and the 529, Daniel the card and the student loan; speak to both (persona D5).
